name: Solstice-Mirage
description: Solstice-Mirage is a study in scale: dust seas the color of old rust roll from pole to pole, interrupted only by the Meridian Rift, a canyon system so vast its far wall is invisible and it weathers its own clouds. At dusk the dune crests glow amber while the rift floor falls into purple darkness, and the temperature swings a hundred and eighty degrees between noon and midnight.

The thin air whistles through the canyon mouths at sundown—a sound the first colonists named the Evening Choir. Sand gets into everything, singing softly as the wind moves it, and the light has a copper warmth that makes even wrecked machinery look gilded. Nights are brutal, silent, and brilliant with stars.

Forty years ago the Solstice Terraforming Compact deployed eleven atmospheric processors the size of cities; today they stand half-buried in dunes, and no two accounts agree on why the project failed. The abandoned colony of New Halcyon remains perfectly preserved under glass—meals on tables, suits racked by the doors—as if three thousand people stepped out one morning and never came back. Their tracks lead toward the ancient impact crater and stop.

Beneath the crater rim, prospectors have found native microbial mats thriving in brine pockets that the terraformers never touched—which suggests life was here before anyone's arrival. The processors could be restarted for a fraction of their original cost, and four governments are bidding to do exactly that. Nobody has yet explained the tracks.
